scenes.narration: Anyone can connect a vector database to a language model in twenty lines of code. But in production, naive vector retrieval fails. You face eight-second tail latencies, permission leaks of confidential documents, and semantic drift. Toy RAG is a demo. Production RAG is a distributed systems problem.

visual.title: PRODUCTION RAG vs TOY DEMOS
visual.subtitle: The gap between Jupyter prototypes and enterprise production systems
items: - Unbounded P99 latency spikes over 8.4 seconds
- Document ACL leakage (Confidential compensation & HR data exposed)
- Semantic drift returning outdated 2022 drafts instead of audited filings
- Asynchronous Event-Driven Ingestion with Parent-Child chunking
- Zero-Trust ACL filters injected directly into vector queries
- Two-stage hybrid search combined with Cross-Encoder re-ranking

scenes.narration: To solve this, we separate our system into two completely decoupled planes. On the left, our Asynchronous Ingestion Plane uses queues to extract structures and index security metadata out of band. On the right, our Query Plane authenticates identity claims before dispatching pre-filtered hybrid queries to the index.

scenes.narration: Building for production means treating AI not as a black-box novelty, but as a component within a disciplined distributed architecture. The companion GitHub repository and Terraform definitions are available in the description below.

visual.title: ARCHITECTURAL TAKEAWAYS
visual.subtitle: Core requirements for senior engineering teams shipping GenAI
items: [+] 1. Decoupled Ingestion: Heavy parsing and OCR must never run synchronously in APIs
[+] 2. Hybrid Search (RRF): Combine keyword precision with semantic embeddings
[+] 3. Zero-Trust Retrieval: Enforce authorization groups at the search engine boundary
[+] 4. Two-Stage Re-Ranking: Eliminate vector noise with cross-encoders before prompt packing
[+] 5. Resilient Orchestration: Safeguard LLM calls with circuit breakers and fallback defaults
